journal.title: Every entry has a history.
journal.subtitle: Originals, derivations and corrections stay traceable together. Append-only.
journal.historyNote: Superseded entries remain visible. An answer uses the latest known state; the original stays.
journal.appendOnlyNote: Journal entries are never edited or deleted. Corrections append new entries that reference what they supersede.
journal.binaryEvidence: Binary content — available through the evidence content endpoint only.

evidenceReason.policy:customer_communication_redacted: Redacted by policy: customer communication content is not retained in the journal.

entity.subtitle: Current state and complete history from the journal.
entity.historyIntro: Newest first. Superseded entries stay visible.
entity.noHistory: No journal entries for this entity.

semantics.invoice: Outstanding = original gross − corrections − bank-evidenced payments. A “paid” marker from the invoicing tool is not cash; a credit note is not a refund.
semantics.transaction: Authorization is not capture. Provider balance, in-transit payout and bank receipt are separate positions; a payout is not revenue.
semantics.order: Ordered, shipped and returned quantities are separate. A return is not an automatic restock.
semantics.item: Available = physical − committed − reserved − damaged − safety stock − quality control. Incoming supply never fills current stock.
semantics.default: Values come from the deterministic engine at the shown cutoff.

entity.noState: No projection exists for this entity yet (no journal entry references it).

order-01.q: Can I still sell 100 Olive Cups?
order-01.method: Subtract active reservations from physical stock. Show promised receipts separately until goods have actually been received.
order-01.need: Item ID, stock snapshot, active reservations and open supply commitments.
order-01.result: Available quantity, shortfall and evidence for the current state.

order-02.q: Which open orders can be fulfilled entirely from available stock?
order-02.method: Check each open line against stock and allocated reservations. Allocate the same units to only one order.
order-02.need: Open order lines, reservation allocations and current stock per warehouse.
order-02.result: Orders classified as fully fulfillable, partially fulfillable or blocked, with reasons.

order-03.q: Which orders have a mismatch between promised and reserved quantities?
order-03.method: Compare the current order quantity with active reservations per line. Account for canceled and shipped quantities.
order-03.need: Order changes, lines, reservations, cancellations and recorded shipments.
order-03.result: Variance per order and line, including missing or excess quantities.

order-04.q: Which open orders are affected by a delayed incoming delivery?
order-04.method: Link the changed receipt commitment to open customer orders through items and allocations. Mark the impact as unresolved where allocations are missing.
order-04.need: Versioned receipt commitment, item links, order allocations and customer deadlines.
order-04.result: Affected orders and commitments at risk, for manual review.

delivery-01.q: Where are my parcels, and which need attention?
delivery-01.method: Combine the latest carrier status with the order, scan time and reported forecast. Keep older scans visible in history.
delivery-01.need: Order-to-shipment links, carrier scans and available delivery forecasts.
delivery-01.result: Shipment overview with last known status and issues requiring attention.

delivery-02.q: Which customer delivery commitments are overdue or at risk?
delivery-02.method: Compare the customer commitment with actual shipping or delivery status. Label carrier forecasts as estimates.
delivery-02.need: Explicit customer commitment, time zone, shipment status and any carrier forecast.
delivery-02.result: Prioritized cases with the promised date, current state and explanation.

delivery-03.q: Which partial deliveries still have missing items?
delivery-03.method: Compare ordered quantities per line with confirmed partial deliveries. Handle canceled lines and shipping labels without shipment confirmation separately.
delivery-03.need: Order lines, partial deliveries, included quantities and handover/delivery events.
delivery-03.result: Outstanding quantities per order and the associated shipments.

delivery-04.q: What can I reliably tell this customer about their delivery status?
delivery-04.method: Use the order, latest scans and prior promises to draft a reply. Explicitly leave unknown arrival dates unresolved.
delivery-04.need: Customer-to-order links, carrier history and prior communication.
delivery-04.result: Customer-friendly draft with internal evidence; sending remains a separate action.

invoice-01.method: Calculate each invoice state from its original amount, corrections and reported payments. Do not sum superseded states again.
invoice-01.need: Invoice, correction documents, reported payment status and due date.
invoice-01.result: Outstanding amounts and due dates with an evidence chain; payment markers are not bank evidence.

invoice-02.q: Which orders still need an invoice under our invoicing rule?
invoice-02.method: Evaluate orders against the configured invoicing rule, for example after shipment. Reconcile linked invoices and cancellations.
invoice-02.need: Invoicing rule, order/delivery status, invoice links and complete import coverage.
invoice-02.result: Review list of potentially missing invoices; status remains unknown when data is incomplete.

invoice-03.q: Where does the invoice amount differ from the agreed order amount?
invoice-03.method: Compare lines, quantities, discounts, shipping charges, currency and stated taxes. Account for partial invoices.
invoice-03.need: Versioned order and invoice lines, including partial-invoice references.
invoice-03.result: Amount difference per line with a traceable reconciliation explanation.

invoice-04.q: Which invoices were created but have no evidence of being sent?
invoice-04.method: Link created documents to the invoicing tool's sending event. With incomplete sending data, report missing evidence only.
invoice-04.need: Invoice ID, creation time, sending status and last synchronization time.
invoice-04.result: Documents without sending evidence, including data freshness rather than an unsupported conclusion that they were not sent.

collection-01.q: Which orders are only authorized, actually paid or still awaiting payment?
collection-01.method: Derive the payment state from authorization and capture events; a marker in the shop is not a capture.
collection-01.need: Order, payment transactions with kind and status, currency.
collection-01.result: Orders grouped by paid, authorized only and awaiting, with evidence per transaction.

collection-02.q: Which failed payments have since been completed successfully?
collection-02.method: Group payment attempts per order and detect a later successful capture after a failure.
collection-02.need: All payment attempts per order with time, status and amount.
collection-02.result: Recovered orders versus still-failed orders, without double counting attempts.

collection-03.q: Which invoices have a mismatch between partial payments and the remaining amount?
collection-03.method: Allocate payments to invoices explicitly and compare allocated sums with the current invoice state.
collection-03.need: Invoices, payments, payment allocations and corrections.
collection-03.result: Invoices with over- or under-allocation and the unexplained difference.

collection-04.q: Which due receivables should Finance review today?
collection-04.method: Rank due receivables by age, amount and open clarification cases; exclude cases already in review.
collection-04.need: Due dates, outstanding amounts, allocations, open cases and the reminder policy.
collection-04.result: Prioritized review queue; items with unresolved ambiguity are flagged, not auto-reminded.

settlement-01.q: Where is my money across payment providers?
settlement-01.method: Derive provider positions from the provider ledger: available, in transit and bank-matched are separate scopes.
settlement-01.need: Provider ledger, payouts, bank entries and holds.
settlement-01.result: Money positions per provider account with evidence; a payout is not revenue.

settlement-02.q: Why is the payout lower than captured customer payments?
settlement-02.method: Reconcile captured amounts minus fees, refunds, holds and adjustments to the payout amount.
settlement-02.need: Provider ledger entries belonging to the payout.
settlement-02.result: Gross-to-net explanation per payout with unexplained remainder, if any.

settlement-03.q: Which announced or sent payouts still lack bank evidence?
settlement-03.method: Match payouts to booked bank entries by amount, reference and date window; unmatched payouts stay open.
settlement-03.need: Payouts with status and independent booked bank data.
settlement-03.result: Payouts without bank confirmation and their age.

settlement-04.q: Which amounts are held, and which releases are only announced?
settlement-04.method: List provider holds and distinguish announced releases from completed ones.

reversal-01.q: Which returns are announced, received or already refunded?
reversal-01.method: Follow each return through announcement, receipt, restock decision and refund.
reversal-01.need: Returns, receipts, refunds and optional invoices/tracking.
reversal-01.result: Returns per lifecycle stage; a receipt is not an automatic restock.

reversal-02.q: Which credit notes are missing their corresponding refund?
reversal-02.method: Link credit notes to refund entitlements and completed refunds; a credit note is not a refund.
reversal-02.need: Invoices, credit notes, payments, entitlements and refunds.
reversal-02.result: Credit notes without a completed refund and their age.

reversal-03.q: What still needs correcting in stock, invoicing and payment after a cancellation?
reversal-03.method: Compare the cancellation with reservations, invoices, payments, refunds and receipts to list open steps.
reversal-03.need: Order, allocations, invoices, payments, refunds, entitlements and receipts.
reversal-03.result: Open correction steps per area with evidence.

reversal-04.q: Is there a risk of duplicate repayment through both a refund and a chargeback?
reversal-04.method: Overlap refunds with disputes per transaction and amount; missing dispute coverage keeps the answer partial.
reversal-04.result: Transactions with potential double repayment, or a partial answer when dispute data is missing.

hero.copy: Orders, payments, stock movements. A flight recorder that brings everything together — locally on your Mac — so you and your agents know what is really going on.

window.answerDetail: 112 in stock. 34 committed. With the evidence behind it.
window.footer2: Every event stays. Every answer has a source.

principle.title: One business. Finally one context.
principle.copy: Your shop knows the order. Your warehouse knows the stock. Your payment provider knows the payout. Blackbox connects the story.
principle.step1: Shopify, Shopify Payments, bank CSV and signed typed input deliver events. The original stays, with timestamp.
principle.step2: What is fact, what was promised, what moved and what is reserved? Five parallel tracks make the difference visible.
principle.step3: 24 deterministic templates answer with sources, cutoffs and clearly named gaps — no language model required.

tracks.title: Nothing gets lost. Everything connects.
tracks.copy: A continuous, append-only journal of your business. New events are added. Changes supersede history — they explain it.
tracks.source: The original. Unchanged and with timestamp.
tracks.fact: What we know. Extracted from sources and evidenced.
tracks.commitment: What was promised. With date, status and responsibility.
tracks.movement: What moved. Goods, money and actual changes.
tracks.reservation: What is already bound. Stock, budget and capacity.

questions.title: No guessing. An answer with evidence.
questions.q1: Can I still sell 100 Olive Cups?
questions.q3: Where is my money across providers?
questions.q5: Which returns are not refunded yet?
questions.answerTitle: Yes to 78. For 100 you are short by 22.
questions.answerCopy: 112 Olive Cups are physically in stock. 34 are already committed to open orders. So you can promise 78 more today.
questions.warning: The 80 pieces for 5 November are a supply commitment. They count as stock only after goods receipt.
questions.proof: Example data · cutoff 31 Oct 2026 10:42 · 5 evidence entries

agents.title: One truth. For every one of your agents.
agents.copy: Through MCP your local agent gets the same traceable business context — with its own read-only key, never with your owner key. Cloud-only agents cannot reach your Mac; no tunnel is offered.

install.title: From download to first answer.
install.intro: The archive contains the wrapper, a pinned Compose configuration with prebuilt images and this guide. No Git, Node or Rust toolchain is needed. Nothing is installed globally without your action.
install.prereq1: Apple Silicon Mac (arm64) with a supported macOS version (see release metadata).
install.prereq2: Docker Desktop 4.3x or newer with Compose v2 (or a compatible container runtime). Blackbox does not install it for you.
install.prereq3: About 2 GiB free disk space for images and data; more for your history.
install.step1: Download the archive above, compare the SHA-256 with the value shown, then extract it into a folder of your choice. macOS may ask you to confirm opening a downloaded archive.
install.step2: Reports runtime, ports and storage without changing anything.
install.step3: Creates one workspace and one owner and prints your personal access key once. Save it in a password manager; it grants owner access and must never be given to an agent.
install.step4: Starts the local backend on 127.0.0.1:19180 only. Then open the address in your browser and sign in with your key.
install.step5Title: Stop, restart and update without losing data
install.step5: Closing the browser keeps the backend running. Stop it explicitly, restart later, or upgrade in place — journal, cursors and snapshots are preserved. Upgrade runs a backup preflight first.
install.step6: Setup and runtime logs are retained locally (7 days / 100 MiB) and readable without a login. If the key is lost, reset it on this Mac only.

closing.title: Ready to record?
closing.copy: Download the private preview for your Mac, install it with three commands and ask your first evidence-backed question within minutes.
